email.body:
Dear Operations,

MV VALDA CREST - Rotterdam, Rijnmond Energy Coal Terminal

The coal berth is occupied. The vessel ahead is expected to complete discharge late on 26 Jan. VALDA CREST is next in line, berthing about 27 Jan 0600 UTC, subject to the vessel ahead completing as planned.

We will advise at once if the line-up changes. Please keep us informed of the vessel's ETA.

Best regards,
Operations desk
Maasport Agencies, Rotterdam

result.result:
**Judgement:** Maasport Agencies' berthing time is only qualified — "about 27 Jan 0600 UTC, subject to the vessel ahead completing as planned" — so it is indicative, not firm, and VALDA CREST will likely anchor in line regardless. The noted heavy weather (wind up to Beaufort 8, seas to 6.1 m from astern) ran from 22 Jan evening to 24 Jan and is now astern of the ship (AIS position 23 Jan 08:00 UTC), so the route ahead appears clear.

**Speed advice (voyage optimisation service, simulated figures):** reduce to 8.3 kn, giving arrival at Rotterdam 27 Jan 04:00 UTC, about 31 hours at anchor before the 06:00 berthing, saving an estimated 38.1 t of VLSFO versus the base 12.4 kn. The speed plan checks out — the distance of 763.6 nm at the advised speed arrives before the berth time.

The operator should decide whether to order the reduced speed. On a yes: (a) send a speed instruction to the Master at 8.3 kn with arrival 27 Jan 04:00 UTC, stressing that his judgement for the safety of the ship in the weather ahead comes first; (b) send the ETA notice that `check_notices` says is due — the ETA has moved 31 hours since the last notice, beyond the CP's 12-hour limit — to the agent and receiver, with the new ETA 27 Jan 04:00 UTC; (c) make a voyage management system entry for the port call ETA. Recommend nothing be sent until the operator answers.
